newsitem.title: GERMANY: German builders warn Bonn tax plan endangers jobs.
newsitem.headline: German builders warn Bonn tax plan endangers jobs.

text.p: A coalition of German builders and building workers unions on Tuesday warned Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government that as many as 300,000 construction jobs could be lost as a consequence of Bonn's planned tax reforms.

Should the government carry out plans to cut tax exemptions for building homes, construction output would decline by some 30 billion marks a year. As a result 150,000 fewer homes would be built, five organisations said in a joint statement in Bonn.
"If this is carried out the continued construction of rental housing is substantially endangered," the statement said.
Bonn's tax reform plans envisage abolishing depreciation of new rental housing, which has allowed investors to write off up to 45 percent of building costs over a 10-year period.

The depreciation exemption for new rental housing is just one of the many tax write-offs the government wants to get rid of in order to finance huge income tax cuts that could take effect as early as next year.

The statement was signed by the Federation of Independent Housing Companies (BFW), Federation of German Trade Unions (DGB), German Tenants' Association (DMB), Federation of German Housing Companies (GdW) and the German Building Workers' Union.

The organisations said that in light of the weak economic situation a sudden change in tax rules would have largely negative consequences for jobs and housing construction in the mid-term and urged the government to consider alternatives.
The changes could also drive rental prices up about five marks per square metre compared to current prices to an average 23 marks in order for investors to cover their costs.
